programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.desc: Luke arrives in Saigon for a breakfast of iced coffee with condensed milk and a vermicelli noodle dish. Later, he visits his favorite Pho restaurant, then cooks up some spicy Chili Crab Claws.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.desc: Luke continues his street food journey in Bangkok where he searches for the best Tom Yum soup and entertains the locals with a rare Thai delicacy.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.sub-title: Malaysian Flying Noodles and Pork Bone Soup
programme.desc: In Kuala Lumpur, Luke meets the famous Mr Hung with a reputation for flying instant noodles and Mr Sou who cooks a hearty Pork Bone Soup with medicinal herbal properties.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Street Food Asia
programme.desc: Luke continues his street food adventure exploring Jakarta, a melting pot of diverse cultural cuisines, where he indulges in an Indonesian dessert, the sweet Martabak, known as the "King of Street Food".

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Railway Vietnam
programme.sub-title: Secret Family Recipies in Ho Chi Minh
programme.desc: Luke searches to find Ho Chi Minh's old markets before they disappear due to District 1's rapid development. Join Luke as he gathers fresh ingredients from a local market, tries some traditional delicacies, and follows his sweet tooth to Marou.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Railway Vietnam
programme.desc: Luke's next stop is the destination of Dalat. Follow Luke as he visits the Art Deco Dalat Train Station, experiences the French influence of the region with a father and son chef duo, and discovers why Dalat is known as the "Land of Eternal Spring"!

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's Railway Vietnam
programme.sub-title: Exploring The 'Wet Market' Of Nha Trang
programme.desc: Luke hops on the train in Ga Thap Cham, and finds himself in Nha Trang—a region of Vietnam with a similar vibe to the French Riviera! Luke hand-catches seafood, looks for some fresh durian fruit, and visits a barramundi farm to harvest sea grapes!

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.sub-title: From Stones to Bronze: Prehistoric Spain
programme.desc: The origins of human settlement on the Iberian Peninsula; learning how the rich spiritual life of early hunters in Spain is reflected in the cave paintings; studying the geography of the peninsula; discovering the extraordinary megalithic tombs.

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.desc: Tracing the impact of the Celts and the technology they bring to the region; learning about the Phoenicians and their legacy of trade and engineering; the singular influence of the Greeks, who shape the history and culture of the peninsula.

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.desc: Tracking the Punic Wars between Rome and Carthage; observing how Rome joins the Iberian provinces together and creates thriving cities; learning about the marvels of Roman engineering, infrastructure, and mining, through which Spain grew rich.

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.desc: Learning about early Christian communities in Spain; charting the role of Spanish churchmen in the establishment of the Roman Catholic Church; how pagan practices are transformed into Christian ones; how Spain becomes a bulwark of church orthodoxy.

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.desc: Germanic and Iranian tribal groups besiege Spanish territories; taking the measure of these people and the new innovations they bring; observing how they partition and rule; how their culture keeps them separate from Spain's Roman population.

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.desc: Learning how the Goths penetrate Roman territories; studying the structure of Visigoth society, which gave rise to influential legal codes and monasticism; Toledo as a center of learning; the diffusion of Visigothic scholarship and culture.

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.desc: The founding of Islam by Muhammad (PBUH); its five tenets; how the new religion spreads with astonishing speed; witnessing the Muslim invasion that conquers most of Spain; observing how the invaders rule, coexisting with Jews and Christians.

programme.title: The History of Spain: Land on a Crossroad
programme.desc: Internal divisions in the Muslim world shape Islamic rule of Spain; investigating issues concerning the larger governance of Islam that leads to enmity between Muslim Spain and the Caliphate in Baghdad; the founding of the Caliphate of Cordoba.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.desc: Learning how history's greatest colonial empire comes about; previewing the roles played by military power, trade, slavery, industrialization and many other forces in motivating Britain to acquire, maintain and ultimately relinquish its empire.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.sub-title: The Challenge to Spain in the New World
programme.desc: Britannia does not always rule the waves; how jealousy over Spanish and Portuguese wealth combines with religious rivalry and advances in nautical knowledge to push England toward its own role in the New World.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.sub-title: African Slavery and the West Indies
programme.desc: Although a more enlightened Britain does away with the African slave trade and slavery, it originally looks at the issue as strictly economic; grasping slavery's importance to not only Britain's New World colonies but to its entire economy.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.desc: Granted a monopoly by the queen in 1600, the British East India Company has no intention of becoming the political overlord of India for its first 150 years; how circumstances override that intention and set the stage for British rule.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.sub-title: Clive and the Conquest of India
programme.desc: How a young officer named Robert Clive, who initially attempts to quell local instability, wins a succession of victories that quickly earn him fame, power and ill-gotten wealth; his actions lay the foundation for British domination of India.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.sub-title: Wolfe and the Conquest of Canada
programme.desc: Britain's victory over the French in the Seven Years' War redraws the world's map in Britain's favor, including control over Canada; this comes at a great cost; the debt is so massive that it contributes to England losing her American colonies.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.sub-title: The Loss of the American Colonies
programme.desc: Britain's desperate need for revenue ends years of "benign neglect" of its prosperous American colonies; colonial resentment of "taxation without representation" triggers the American Revolution that inflicts a defeat on the empire.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
programme.desc: The path to Britain's empire is marked by great strides in exploration, invention and science; how accelerating scientific knowledge connects directly to British exploration, mapping and colonization of previously remote areas of the world.

programme.title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Why Study Battles? What Is War?
programme.desc: Garrett G. Fagan addresses the importance of studying battles and surveys the changing scholarly approach to the subject; he concludes by looking at different definitions of warfare, particularly the operational and social-constructivist models.

programme.title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Three types of evidence shed light on the origins of warfare; human remains bearing evidence of trauma; artifacts that function primarily as weapons; fortifications or depictions of warriors painted on cave walls; their interpretations are tricky.

programme.title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Sumer, Akkad, and Early Mesopotamian Warfare
programme.desc: Written records first become available in the historical era; evidence reconstructs the conventions and conditions of warfare among the first cities in Sumer circa the 30th century B.C.; exploring the nature of Sumerian armies and battle tactics.

programme.title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Egyptian Warfare From the Old to New Kingdoms
programme.desc: Evidence of warfare in Ancient Egypt is ambiguous, but it is much more plentiful in later periods; the pharaoh's role is increasingly that of a war leader; Egyptian warfare is transformed by the introduction of the chariot.

programme.title: The History of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: Knowing what makes Ancient Egypt so interesting; how one knows what one knows about it; understanding what can one, as a student, expect from these lectures.

programme.title: The History of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: Seeing just how old 'old' is; the basic divisions of prehistory are discussed; each category is defined and its specific characteristics delineated; once these categories are clear, discussing the difficulties of studying a prehistoric civilization.

programme.title: The History of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: Knowing what distinguishes mythology, religion and philosophy from one another; understanding the role did each plays in the lives of the ancient Egyptians.

programme.title: The History of Ancient Egypt
programme.sub-title: Napoleon and the Beginnings of Egyptology
programme.desc: Knowing why modern Egyptology begins with Napoleon; how is Egypt studied before he and his army arrive with 150 scientists in tow in 1798; the Description de l'Egypte that Bonaparte's savants produce becomes a benchmark for future publications.
